name: Rosewood Luang Prabang
positioning: Bill Bensley-designed riverside hideaway of rooms, villas and hilltop tents set among waterfalls outside Luang Prabang
best_for: Couples wanting a secluded waterfall setting with hilltop tents
Travelers who want Lao culture, local food and heritage experiences

facts.text: The hotel is in Nauea Village, in a wild enclave outside Luang Prabang.
The accommodations sit in a riverside landscape, with natural waterfalls flowing throughout the resort grounds.
The hotel was designed by Bangkok-based architect Bill Bensley.
The Waterfall Pool Villas have private terraces, and the Riverside Villas have a private balcony.
The restaurants combine French and Laotian flavors with seasonally sourced farm-to-table ingredients.
The open-air Great House serves Laotian flavors and Western-inspired dishes made with vegetables and herbs sourced exclusively from local markets and farmers.
The Elephant Bridge Bar is housed over a creek where elephants once roamed and serves cocktails made with local herbs and spices.
Guests can take part in the dawn alms offering as saffron-robed monks walk the streets.
Cultural specialist Francis Engelmann leads a guided architectural walk through Luang Prabang.
Guests can feed, bathe and trek with rescued elephants at the MandaLao Elephant Sanctuary.
The Sense Spa is on the hillside.
The Two-Bedroom Riverside Suite has river views and is described as ideal for family moments.

highlights.text: The Hilltop Tents are a jungle sanctuary perched on a hilltop.
The tents, villas and rooms are all set by the waterfall, so guests fall asleep to the sound of water.
Guests can trek with the chef into neighboring farmland to forage with the Hmong hill tribe for wild herbs.
A Private Waterfall Dinner offers candlelit fine dining with local flavors beside the estate's waterfalls.
The hotel offers sunset river voyages with cocktails and half-day cruises to the Pak Ou Caves.

considerations.text: Reaching the tents means climbing for several minutes at a significant incline, which can be especially challenging in rainy season.
The hotel is outside Luang Prabang rather than in the town itself.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the ultra-high-end positioning.
